description: Hosting the 14th Commonwealth Women's Affairs Ministers Meeting
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-10-26 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Commonwealth Women's Affairs Ministers Meeting is a highlevel international meeting that provides an opportunity for Commonwealth member countries to hold policy dialogues with the aim of promoting gender equality and the empowerment of women, exchange experiences and good practices and strengthen cooperation among member countries. Sri Lanka has agreed to hold its 14th meeting in Sri Lanka. Ministers in charge of the subject of women's affairs of member countries, senior Government officials, representatives of recognized civil society organizations and representatives of relevant stakeholder institutions are scheduled to participate in that meeting. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Women and Child Affairs to host the 14th Commonwealth Women's Affairs Ministers Meeting in Sri Lanka in the first quarter of 2028, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Hosting the Inaugural BIMSTEC Health Ministers' Meeting and BIMSTEC Senior Officials’ Meeting on Health
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-10-26 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation (BIMSTEC) serves as a key regional forum to foster socioeconomic development and technical cooperation among South and Southeast Asian nations. During the 6th BIMSTEC Summit held in Bangkok, Thailand, in April 2025, attention was drawn on convening a BIMSTEC Health Ministers' Meeting to strengthen regional cooperation in the health sector and it has been proposed that this meeting be hosted by Sri Lanka, which has been designated as the Lead Country for Public Health Cooperation within the BIMSTEC. Accordingly, it has been decided to host the Inaugural BIMSTEC Health Ministers’ Meeting and BIMSTEC Senior Officials’ Meeting on Health in Colombo on 10th and 11th November 2026. The proposal made by the Minister of Health and Mass Media to host these meetings, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Imposing Regulations for Registration of Intellectual Property Agents (IP Agents) under the Intellectual Property Act No.36 of 2003
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-10-26 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The provisions of the Intellectual Property Act No.36 of 2003 have made legal provisions for the recognition of IP Agents and the execution of their functions. This Act provides legislative provisions for the recognition of AttorneysatLaw as IP Agents, while also establishing the legal basis for the recognition of nonlawyer individuals and corporate entities as IP Agents. Furthermore, the Intellectual Property Regulations No. 01 of 2006, published through the Gazette Notification No.1445/10 dated 2006-05-17, has authorize the Director General of Intellectual Property to formulate administrative procedures for the registration of such agents and the said Act has also introduced the eligibility criteria for non-lawyers but possess the requisite qualifications to be appointed as IP Agents. Accordingly, the Gazette Extraordinary Notification No.2500/15 dated 2026-08-03 has been published to amend the Regulation 58 of the Intellectual Property Regulations No.01 of 2006 by making provisions for individuals with higher educational qualifications including a Bachelor’s degree in relevant field such as Engineering or Science to act as Agents in matters relating to patents. The proposal made by the Minister of Trade, Commerce, Food Security and Co-operative Development, to present said amending Regulations to Parliament for approval, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Submission of the Licensing of Produce Brokers (Tea) Regulations, to Parliament for approval
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-10-26 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - In accordance with the approval granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2026-06-22, the amended Regulations have been published through the Gazette Extraordinary Notification No. 2501/68 dated 2026-08-12 to amend the Licensing of Produce Brokers (Tea) Regulations, 1979 made under the provisions of the Licensing of Procedure Brokers Act No.09 of 1979. The proposal made by the Minister of Plantation and Community Infrastructure to submit the said amending Regulations to Parliament for approval, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Rehabilitation and improvement of Norwood-Bogawanthalawa - Campion Road (B329) road - from Ch.10+500km to Ch.16+890km
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-10-26 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Bids have been invited following the National Competitive Procurement Procedure, for the rehabilitation and improvement of the section from 10+500 km to 16+890 km of the Norwood-Bogawanthalawa-Campion Road (B329) that has deteriorated due to prolonged exposure to adverse weather conditions and the impact of disasters. Three bids have been submitted for the same. The proposal made by the Minister of Transport, Highways and Urban Development to award the relevant contract to M/s Asset Engineering (Pvt) Ltd., the substantially responsive lowest evaluated bidder, for a sum of Rs.756.99 million (excluding Value Added Tax), based on the recommendations given by the High Level Procurement Committee pertaining to the said bids, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Provision of Compensation and Relief to Prison Officers who tragically lost their lives and sustained injuries while on duty at the Negombo Prison
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-10-26 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body:
- Following the riots that erupted at the Negombo Prison on 05th and 6th July 2026 which resulted in the loss of life and injuries to prison officers on duty, a Committee headed by the Secretary to the Ministry of Justice and National Integration was appointed at the Cabinet meeting held 2026-08-03, to make recommendations pertaining to the provision of compensations and relief. The said Committee has submitted the Report containing its recommendations. Accordingly, the Minister of Justice and National Integration presented the said Report to the Cabinet, and approval was granted to implement the following recommendations contained therein: (i) Payment of a special compensation as follows, in addition to the compensation payable under the provisions of the Public Administration Circular No. 22/93:

Payment of a compensation of Rs. 5 million on behalf of a deceased officer.


Payment of a compensation of Rs. 5 million to a permanently disabled officer.


Payment of compensation amounting to Rs. 4 million to an officer who sustains a partial disability resulting in a 100% loss of maximum earning capacity.


Payment of a compensation of Rs. 3 million to an officer who sustains a temporary partial disability.
(ii) Amending the Prisons Ordinance to include appropriate provisions that grant legal status to the Prisons Tactical Force.(iii) Strengthening the Prisons Tactical Force by recruiting an adequate and suitable number of officers.(iv) Providing formal training in relevant fields to the Prisons Tactical Force and equipping the force with necessary modern equipment.(v) Taking action to establish a Prisons Tactical Force Headquarter at a suitable location.

description: Establishment of the National Wildlife Hazard Management Committee for Aviation Safety
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-10-26 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - As a Contracting State to the Convention on International Civil Aviation (Chicago Convention), Sri Lanka is required to implement applicable Standards and Recommended Practices aimed at minimizing aircraft-wildlife strikes in accordance with the provisions of the said Convention. Specifically, pursuant to Paragraph 9.4 of Volume I, Annex 14 to the Convention on International Civil Aviation, aircraft-wildlife strikes occurring on or in the vicinity of an aerodrome must be assessed with a national procedure for recording and reporting wildlife strikes, collecting information on wildlife that poses a potential hazard and conducting ongoing evaluations by competent personnel. Further, reports concerning aircraft wildlife strikes must be submitted for inclusion in the International Civil Aviation Organization’s (ICAO) Bird Strike Information System. The guidelines for the Asia-Pacific region under the Convention on International Civil Aviation provide for the establishment of a Wildlife Hazard Management Committee or Forum to facilitate action at the national level. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Ports and Civil Aviation to establish the National Wildlife Hazard Management Committee for Aviation Safety representing all relevant stakeholder institutions, as the national coordination mechanism for managing wildlife hazards in relation to civil aviation activities, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Leasing out underutilized lands/properties in plantation sector to suitable investors for optimal utilization
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-10-26 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Approval of the Cabinet has been previously granted to call for Expressions of Interest from interested investors, for leasing out underutilized lands/properties managed by the Sri Lanka State Plantations Corporation, the Janatha Estates Development Board, and the Elkaduwa Plantations Limited to suitable investors with a view to ensuring their optimal utilization. Accordingly, under the first phase, Expressions of Interest have been called for 1,514 hectares of land, 10 tourist bungalows and scenic locations, as well as 15 non-operational factories and as a result 470 interested investors have submitted Expressions of Interest. Subsequently, Requests for Proposals (RFPs) have been invited from the shortlisted investors, and 44 proposals have been received in relation to 30 land/property units. Based on recommendations submitted by the High-Level Procurement Committee, following the evaluation of said proposals, the proposal made by the Minister of Plantation and Community Infrastructure to lease out 15 plots of lands/properties belonging to the Sri Lanka State Plantations Corporation, the Janatha Estates Development Board, and Elkaduwa Plantations Limited to the selected investors on long-term lease basis, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Entering into a Memorandum of Understanding to implement Vocational Training and Student Exchange Programmes
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-10-26 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The National Institute of Occupational Safety and Health, which operates under the Ministry of Labour, has signed a Memorandum of Understanding in 2023 with Changshin University of the Republic of Korea to implement vocational training and student exchange programs. However, the said MoU has not yet been implemented due to issues that arose regarding certain provisions in the said MoU. Therefore, a new Memorandum of Understanding and an Operational Framework involving five key parties have been formulated to establish a formal relationship. Accordingly, the proposed MoU has been prepared aiming to provide Sri Lankan students, selected through the National Institute of Occupational Safety and Health, with the opportunity to pursue higher education at Changshin University in the Republic of Korea and subsequently, to secure employment opportunities within industries located in the Gyeongsangnam-do Province, as well as to avail the possibility of long-term residency in that province. The proposal made by the Minister of Labour to enter into the said Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) and the Operational Framework among the Ministry of Labour of Sri Lanka, the National Institute of Occupational Safety and Health of Sri Lanka, the Gyeongsangnam-do Province of the Republic of Korea, the Sacheon Chamber of Commerce and Industry, and Changshin University, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Holding the 19th World Trade Union Congress in Sri Lanka from 2027-05-13 to 2027-05-15
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-10-26 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - It has been decided to hold the 19th World Trade Union Congress, organized by the World Federation of Trade Unions, in Colombo from 2027-05-13 to 2027-05-15. Considering Sri Lanka’s active trade union sector and strategic location, the Presidential Council of the World Federation of Trade Unions has entrusted the hosting of the said Congress to Sri Lanka. It is expected that approximately 800 delegates from nearly 130 countries, representing trade unions across the globe, will participate in the event. Accordingly, the Minister of Labour informed the Cabinet regarding the hosting of the 19th World Trade Union Congress in Colombo from 2027-05-13 to 2027-05-15 by Sri Lanka and the Cabinet granted its concurrence to proceed with the necessary arrangements.

description: Obtaining Funds from the OPEC Fund for International Development (OFID) for the Mahaweli Water Security Investment Programme - Stage 2
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-10-26 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body:
- It has been planned to implement the Stage 2 of the Mahaweli Water Security Investment Programme to achieve the Government’s long-term objectives such as enhancing food security, strengthening water resource management, improving resilience to climate change, and reducing poverty in the Dry Zone. Accordingly, following tasks are intended to be completed under the said Stage:

Completion of the remaining section of the main tunnel, including approximately 7 kilometres of tunnel excavation and associated finishing works.


Construction of open and covered canals, conduits, and small tunnel sections, spanning a total length of approximately 68 kilometres.


Construction of an approximately 8 kilometre canal section of the Ellapothana Irrigation Project.


Establishment of commercial agricultural development infrastructure for the development of approximately 13 pressure distribution networks to provide a reliable and efficient supply of irrigation water for high-value crops and field crops.


Transformation of agricultural production systems through the introduction of climate-resilient value chains and expansion of access to financial services and agricultural project-related services for farmers.

As the total estimated cost for Stage 2 of the Mahaweli Water Security Investment Programme is US$ 536.5 million, it has been proposed to secure the necessary funding through a co-financing arrangement with multiple development partners. Accordingly, the Asian Development Bank has already agreed to provide US$ 200 million for this project. At the Cabinet meeting held on 2026-07-20, approval was granted to conduct negotiations with the OFID to secure US$ 60 million in funding as part of the proposed co-financing arrangement. Subsequent to said negotiations, the OFID has expressed its willingness to provide a loan facility consisting of two components viz US$ 48 million and US$ 12 million. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. President, in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning, and Economic Development to enter into an Agreement with the OFID to secure a loan facility of US$ 60 million for the said project, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Performance and Sustainability Oriented Framework for Collective Agreements in State-Owned Enterprises
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-10-26 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - It has been decided at the Cabinet meeting held on 2026-05-11 to extend the existing Collective Agreements in State-Owned Enterprises under their current terms and conditions until 2026-12-31, to develop a new, revised framework to be effective from 2027-01-01 and to appoint an Expert Committee to review the existing Collective Agreement Mechanism and formulate the said revised framework. Accordingly, the Secretary to the Treasury has appointed an Expert Committee, and the said Committee in consultation with the relevant parties as well, has submitted a Report titled 'Performance and Sustainability Oriented Framework for Collective Agreements in State-Owned Enterprises' The Report has made recommendations regarding the implementation of Collective Agreements in State-Owned Enterprises in compliance with the Industrial Disputes Act, the Trade Unions Ordinance, the Shop and Office Employees laws, and other relevant labour laws and made recommendations regarding a framework for profit-sharing and bonuses. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. President, in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development, to implement the new policy framework applicable to the Collective Agreement Mechanism in State-Owned Enterprises, with effect from January 2027-01-01, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Obtaining financial assistance from the Asian Development Bank for the implementation of Promoting Resilience and Opportunity for Inclusive Recovery Sector Development Programme
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-10-26 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Approval has been granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2026-03-16 to obtain a policy-based loan of US$ 620 million from the Asian Development Bank (ADB) structured under five sub programmes in order to advance Sri Lanka’s reform agenda in line with the Extended Fund Facility (EFF) programme of the International Monetary Fund and conduct loan negotiations with the ADB for the same. Also, approval has been granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2026-09-07 to implement the Promoting Resilience and Opportunity for Inclusive Recovery Sector Development Programme, utilizing US$ 100 million from the said loan facility. The Department of External Resources has concluded formal loan negotiations with the Asian Development Bank in respect of obtaining the said loan. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. President, in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development, to enter into an agreement with the Asian Development Bank to obtain the said loan comprising of a policy-based loan component of US$ 50 million and an investment loan component of US$ 50 million provided through the Regular Ordinary Capital Resources of the Asian Development Bank, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Conducting the cremation ceremony of the late Anunayake Thero of the Sri Lanka Ramagngna Maha Nikaya, Chief Incumbant of the Gatambe Rajopawanaramaya, Most Venerable Kappitiyagoda Siriwimalabhidhana Anunayaka Thero, with State Partonage
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-10-19 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The cremation ceremony of the Anunayake Thero of the Sri Lanka Ramagngna Maha Nikaya, Chief Incumbant of the Peradeniya Gatambe Rajopawanaramaya, Sri Chandawimala Wansalankara, Chandakeerthi Sri Amarawansa Saddarma Vagheswara shasanahobhaana Most Venerable Kappitiyagoda Siriwimalabhidhana Anunayaka Thero who passed away on 2026-10-18 is scheduled to be held on 2026-10-21, at the Gatambe Municipal Council Grounds. The joint proposal made by the Minister of Public Administration, Provincial Councils and Local Government; and the Minister of Buddhasasana, Religious and Cultural Affairs to conduct the said cremation ceremony under state patronage, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Establishment of the National High-Performance Centre
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-10-19 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - It has been identified that, although Sri Lankan athletes possess exceptional talent, the absence of a cohesive, scientifically-grounded 'high-performance' sports system capable of transforming these talents into consistent international-level performance, serves as a major barrier for enhancing Sri Lanka’s competitiveness in international sport events, including the Olympic Games. Accordingly, a Committee comprising of experts in relevant fields has been appointed to provide recommendations for the establishment of a basic High-Performance Centre. Based on the recommendations submitted by the said Committee, plans have been made to establish the 'National High-Performance Centre' in Diyagama area under an estimated cost of Rs.3,980 million within a time period of 03 years from the year 2027, with the objective of boosting Sri Lanka’s competitiveness in upcoming international sport events, as well as in the Olympic Games 2028, 2032, and 2036. It has been decided that, it would be appropriate to initiate a National High-Performance Centre by utilizing the infrastructure available at the Torrington Stand of the Torrington Sports Ground and the Institute of Sports Medicine, until the proposed Diyagama 'National High-Performance Centre is established, in order to provide the necessary facilities to enhance the performance of elite-level athletes identified focusing the upcoming international sports competitions and the Olympic Games 2028. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Youth Affairs and Sports to pursue action pertaining to the establishment of the proposed National High-Performance Centre, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of functions of the Presidential Welfare Fund for Performing Artists by the Tower Hall Theatre Foundation
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-10-19 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The operations of the Presidential Welfare Fund for Performing Artists, a nonstatutory fund maintained by the Tower Hall Theatre Foundation, have to be concluded in accordance with the provisions of the Public Finance Management Act, No. 44 of 2024. Accordingly, the Cabinet, having been informed by the Minister of Buddhasasana, Religious and Cultural Affairs that steps will be taken to invest the sum of Rs.80.8 million currently held under the said Fund through the Tower Hall Theatre Foundation Account and that the income generated from this investment will be utilized to ensure the continued implementation of the ongoing programme for providing a monthly living allowance to elderly artists, decided to grant its concurrence for the same.

description: Amendment of the Sri Lanka Institute of Development Administration Act No.9 of 1982
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-10-19 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Cabinet, at its meeting held on 2018-08-28, granted approval to amend the Sri Lanka Institute of Development Administration Act, No.9 of 1982 by incorporating necessary amendments to formulate the functions and administrative structure of the Sri Lanka Institute of Development Administration to suit the present-day requirements. The Legal Draftsman is currently in the process of preparing the relevant Bill and the proposal submitted by the Minister of Public Administration, Provincial Councils and Local Government to grant policy approval of the Cabinet for the finalization of drafting the said amendments, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendment of the Ayurveda Act, No. 31 of 1961
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-10-19 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The regulation, development and administration of the indigenous medicine sector in Sri Lanka comprising of Ayurveda, Siddha, Unani, and indigenous traditional medicine systems (Desiya Chikitsa) are carried out in accordance with the provisions of the Ayurveda Act, No.31 of 1961. Although the relevant Act has been amended from time to time as required, it has now been found necessary to further amend the Ayurveda Act by introducing timely amendments to facilitate the effective and efficient conduct of all activities within the indigenous medicine sector, streamline the regulatory functions of the said sector, issue licenses relating to the export of indigenous medicinal products and achieve the overall progress of the indigenous medicine sector as well as the sustainable development goals. The proposal made by the Minister of Health and Mass Media to instruct the Legal Draftsman to prepare a Bill to amend the Ayurveda Act, No.31 of 1961 based on the aforesaid matters, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Public Private Partnership Bill
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-10-19 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Cabinet, at its meeting held on 2025-06-02, granted approval for the introduction of a new Act to establish the National Agency for Public Private Partnership and to provide the legal provisions for promoting and facilitating Public Private Partnerships in Sri Lanka. Accordingly, the relevant Bill has been drafted by the Legal Draftsman, and legal clearance has been granted by the Attorney General for the same. The proposal made by the Hon. President, in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning, and Economic Development, to publish the said Bill in the Government Gazette and submit the same thereafter to Parliament for approval, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Imports and Exports (Control) Regulations No.08 of 2026
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-10-19 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - With the objective of ensuring a fair competitive environment for domestic manufacturers, as well as guaranteeing consumer protection and safety, the Ministry of Industries and Entrepreneurship Development has recommended the application of the import inspection scheme i.e. Sri Lanka Standards for imported tyres used for passenger cars and pneumatic tyres for three wheeled vehicles. Taking into account this recommendation, the 'Import and Export (Control) Regulations No. 08 of 2026' have been imposed through Gazette Extraordinary Notification No. 2508/27 dated 2026-10-01 to amend the existing Regulations, by prescribing the Sri Lanka Standard 1212 for the import of passenger car tyres (HS Code 4011.10.90) and the Sri Lanka Standard 1347 for the import of pneumatic tyres for three wheeled vehicles (HS Code 4011.90.10). Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. President, in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development, to present the said Regulations to Parliament for approval, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Purchase of 200 Single Cabs for the Sri Lanka Police
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-10-19 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Approval was granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2026-02-23 for the procurement of 200 imported single cabs from the local market for the duties of the Sri Lanka Police. Accordingly, bids have been invited following the National Competitive Procurement Procedure, and 07 bids have been submitted for the same. The proposal made by the Minister of Public Security and Parliamentary Affairs to purchase 200 single cabs (TATA YODHA PICKUP) from M/s Diesel and Motor Engineering PLC, the substantially responsive lowest evaluated bidder, at a price of Rs.4,785,000/- per vehicle (excluding Value Added Tax), based on the recommendation submitted by the High Level Procurement Committee subsequent to evaluation of the said bids, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Project for the Construction of an Official Quarters Complex with 200 Housing Units for Public Officers in the Ratnapura New Town
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-10-19 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - During the Ratnapura District Coordinating Committee meeting held on 2025-10-14, chaired by the Hon. President, it has been proposed to construct a Housing Complex with 200 housing units for Public Officers on a land belonging to the Urban Development Authority in the Ratnapura New Town in place of the Government Official Quarters located in Colin Crescent area. Further, it has also been decided to transfer the State-owned land where the official quarters are located at present to the Urban Development Authority and utilize them more effectively for future development activities. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Transport, Highways and Urban Development to implement the project for the construction of the relevant official quarters complex with 200 housing units, under an estimated cost of Rs.5,886.97 million, over a period of 05 years, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Kolonnawa Stromwater Drainage and Environment Improvement Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-10-19 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body:
- Although construction activities of the Kolonnawa Stormwater Drainage and Environmental Improvement Project commenced in 2019, the implementation of its components as originally planned was disrupted due to the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020 and the subsequent economic crisis faced by Sri Lanka. Consequently, a new project plan and a corresponding cost estimate have been prepared for the remaining tasks. The proposal made by the Minister of Transport, Highways, and Urban Development to implement the project activities according to the new project plan over a period of three years, at an estimated cost of Rs.15,077.82 million under the following key components, was approved by the Cabinet:

Completion of the ongoing Selalihini Mawatha canal (3,250 meters) and construction of the Dahamwela canal (3,868 meters).


Execution of specialized works, such as the development of water ponds/water retention areas.


Rehabilitation of the Passenna canal (4,475 meters) and the Danduthota canal (650 meters), Danduthota sluice gate, and installation of three mobile pumps, each with a capacity to pump 1 cubic meter of rainwater per second.


Acquisition of land plots within the project area that should be essentially acquired for the implementation of the project, and the implementation of a concessionary allowance scheme estimated at Rs.1,015 million for affected families, taking into consideration the potential impact on their daily livelihoods.

description: Project for the construction of two (02) Wastewater Treatment Plants for the service area at the Welipenna of the Southern Expressway
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-10-19 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Canowin Hotels & Spas (Private) Limited, a fully owned subsidiary of                    Sri Lanka Insurance Corporation, operates the service area located in the Welipenna area of the Southern Expressway. It has been identified that the capacity of the existing wastewater treatment plants at the said service area is insufficient. The National Water Supply and Drainage Board has examined the situation and submitted a Report recommending the construction of two (02) new wastewater treatment plants, each with a capacity of 200 cubic meters per day. Accordingly, the proposal made by the President, in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development, to award the contract for the construction of two (02) wastewater treatment plants at the Welipenna service area, to the National Water Supply and Drainage Board at an estimated cost of Rs.562.04 million, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Transfer of the premises of the SAARC Cultural Centre in Navimana, Matara, to the Ministry of Education, Higher Education and Vocational Education to house the Sri Lanka Ocean University
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-10-19 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - At the Cabinet meeting held on 2026-06-01, it has been decided to instruct the Secretary to the Ministry of Education, Higher Education, and Vocational Education to explore the possibility of utilizing the buildings and premises of the SAARC Cultural Centre in Navimana, Matara, for educational or vocational training purposes. Accordingly, it has been identified that it would be appropriate to transfer the SAARC Cultural Centre, situated on an 11-acre plot of land and comprising a partially completed building complex with a floor area of 200,000 square feet, to the Ocean University of Sri Lanka to house the said University, which currently operates in several rented buildings. The concurrence of the Ministry of Buddhasasana, Religious and Cultural Affairs has been received for the purpose. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in her capacity as the Minister of Education, Higher Education, and Vocational Education to transfer the premises of the SAARC Cultural Centre in Navimana, Matara, to the Ministry of Education, Higher Education, and Vocational Education to house the Ocean University of Sri Lanka, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Vesting of the Nippon Mawatha in Ethulkotte, in the                                                   Sri Jayewardenepura Kotte Municipal Council
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-10-19 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The cross road connecting Sri Jayewardenepura Mawatha to Beddagana Road passing through the Beddagana Biodiversity Park was constructed by the Urban Development Authority and is known as Nippon Mawatha. At the Cabinet meeting held on 2008-07-02, approval has been granted to transfer a section of the Nippon Mawatha extending from the Mahindarama Temple to Beddagana, to the Sri Jayewardenepura Kotte Municipal Council via a free grant, for maintenance and upkeep. Furthermore, in response to the requests from local residents seeking the proper maintenance of the remaining portion of the Nippon Mawatha extending from Sri Jayewardenepura Mawatha to the Sri Sunethrarama Viharaya, it has been decided at the Divisional Coordinating Committee meeting held on 2025-03-12, to transfer this section as well to the Sri Jayewardenepura Kotte Municipal Council. The approval of the Board of Management of the Urban Development Authority has also been received for the said transfer. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Transport, Highways, and Urban Development to transfer the relevant road section in extent of 02 acres, 02 roods, and 31 perches to the Sri Jayewardenepura Municipal Council as a free grant, for maintenance and upkeep, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Adopting the Credit Risk Assessment Methodology for financial institutions under the provisions of the Public Debt Management Act, No.33 of 2024
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-10-19 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Approval of the Cabinet has been granted previously for the credit risk assessment methodology developed by the Public Debt Management Office to assess risk associated on the issuance of loan guarantees or on-lending to State-Owned Enterprises, in accordance with the provisions of the Public Debt Management Act, No.33 of 2024. The Central Bank of Sri Lanka and financial institutions whose business is partly or fully into lending or borrowing have been excluded from the definition of State-Owned Enterprise as stipulated in the Public Debt Management Act. Therefore, taking into consideration of the distinctive nature of financial institutions, higher degree of leverage, liquidity and market risks, regulatory requirements and their potential systematic importance, the necessity of developing an appropriate methodology to assess the credit risk of those institutions in relation to the issuance of loan guarantees or on-lending has been identified. The Public Debt Management Office has developed Credit Risk Assessment Methodology for financial institutions, based on credit ratings assigned to them by the authorized credit rating agencies operating in Sri Lanka. Accordingly, the Cabinet of Ministers has approved a proposal presented by the President, in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development to adopt this methodology for assessing the credit risk of financial institutions in Sri Lanka.

description: Implementation of the Suraksha Student Insurance Programme for the year 2026/27
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-10-19 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body:
- The Suraksha Student Insurance Programme has been launched with the primary objective of creating an environment that enables students whose education is disrupted due to various health issues to overcome these obstacles and continue their studies without interruption. Students studying in government schools, government-approved private schools, Pirivenas, and assisted special schools are eligible to receive benefits under the said programme. The Hon. Prime Minister, in her capacity as the Minister of Education, Higher Education, and Vocational Education, informed the Cabinet that steps will be taken to amend and implement the existing Agreement between the Ministry of Education, Higher Education, and Vocational Education and Sri Lanka Insurance Corporation General Limited pertaining to the implementation of the said Student Insurance Programme, including the following new benefits as well, covering the period from 2026-09-01 to 2027-08-31, and the Cabinet decided to grant its concurrence for the same:

Providing the opportunity to obtain benefits up to Rs.75,000/- for the repair of hearing accessories and related service charges.


Providing the opportunity to obtain benefits up to Rs.20,000/- for students receiving long-term medication for Chronic Kidney Disease and Chronic Inflammatory Arthritis.


Providing the opportunity to obtain benefits up to Rs.20,000/- to cover the costs incurred for Malignancy Screening Test for Skin Cancer and Post-transplant Lymphoproliferative Disorder (PLTD), Screening Test for Osteoporosis and Screening Test for Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C and HIV Test.


Amending the term 'Cancer Treatment' listed under the Critical Illness category as 'Cancer Treatment and related Testing', and covering expenses for major surgeries for hip, shoulder, and knee joint replacement due to accidents as well as PET scans under the critical illness category.


Providing the opportunity to obtain benefits up Rs.100,000/- under the category of accidents in the event of student deaths resulting from accidents within or outside the school premises during activities (educational field trips and sports events etc.) that are organized by institutions under the purview of the Ministries of Education, Higher Education, or Vocational Education, and conducted under the supervision of educational authorities.

description: Appointment to the Post of Director General of the Department of Technical Education and Training
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-10-12 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Approval has been granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2026-01-26, to appoint Mrs. Dilki Wathsala Marambage, Grade I Officer of the Sri Lanka Administrative Service, to the post of Director General of the Department of Technical Education and Training on full-time acting basis. She has been promoted to the Special Grade of the Sri Lanka Administrative Service by the Public Service Commission, from 2026-01-01. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in her capacity as the Minister of Education, Higher Education, and Vocational Education to appoint Mrs. Dilki Wathsala Marambage to the post of Director General of the Department of Technical Education and Training on permanent basis, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amending the Co-operative Employees Commission Act, No.12 of 1972
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-10-12 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The need to amend the Co-operative Employees Commission Act No. 12 of 1972 has been identified, taking into account the need to align the functioning of co-operative societies with the current socio-economic conditions and changes in the general law. The Co-operative Employees Commission has prepared an initial draft containing proposed amendments, based on the views and proposals of co-operative societies, members of their boards of directors, co-operative employees, and other interested parties, as well as on the experience gained by the Commission. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Trade, Commerce, Food Security, and Co-operative Development to instruct the Legal Draftsman to prepare a Bill to amend the Co-operative Employees Commission Act No.12 of 1972, based on the said initial draft, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Public Assets Management Act
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-10-12 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Approval has been granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2024-07-22, to publish the Public Assets Management Bill in the Government Gazette and subsequently submit it to Parliament for approval. However, the Bill could not be passed in Parliament due to its dissolution in October 2024. Subsequently, a Committee comprising of Officials and experts in the relevant field was appointed to further review the Bill. The said Committee has identified necessary amendments to be made to the Bill and prepared a preliminary draft incorporating the proposed changes. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. President, in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development, to suspend further action regarding the Public Assets Management Bill published in the Gazette Extraordinary Notification dated 2024-08-02, and to instruct the Legal Draftsman to prepare a bill based on the initial draft formulated by the Committee of Experts in the relevant field, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Integrated One Health Pandemic Preparedness and Response Strengthening Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-10-12 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Sri Lanka has achieved remarkable progress in controlling communicable diseases and delivering maternal and child healthcare services. Furthermore, the country has made significant strides in the prevention and control of vaccine-preventable diseases, maintaining a vaccination coverage rate exceeding 95%. Sri Lanka has signed an Agreement on 2025-03-20 to secure a grant from the Pandemic Fund, a collaborative partnership involving donor nations, co-investors, foundations, and civil organizations. Under the terms of the said Agreement, all activities related to the grant must be fully implemented and concluded by 2028-03-31. Sri Lanka's response to the COVID-19 pandemic and other public health emergencies due to zoonotic diseases has revealed deficiencies and gaps in the national response across both the human and animal health sectors. Activities proposed to address these gaps are set to be implemented through the Pandemic Fund, and an action plan covering the 2026-2028 period has also been formulated in collaboration with funding organizations. The said plan also includes key infrastructure development activities, such as the establishment of the Sri Lanka Center for Disease Control and Prevention and the upgrading of physical infrastructure at the National Public Health Reference Laboratory of the Medical Research Institute. Funding for the establishment of the Center for Disease Control and Prevention is expected to be provided by the Asian Development Bank. Accordingly, the Cabinet approved the proposal made by the Minister of Health and Mass Media to implement 35 identified activities including the upgrading of the physical infrastructure at the National Public Health Reference Laboratory of the Medical Research Institute, utilizing the total provisions of Rs.5,431 million, comprising a grant of Rs.4,785 million obtained under the Health Pandemic and Response Strengthening Project and a contribution of Rs.646 million from the Government of Sri Lanka.

description: Awarding the contract for widening and improvement of the Kandy - Jaffna Road (A0009) (CH 58+240km to CH 63+000 km)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-10-12 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Under the Widening and Improvement Programme of National Highways, bids have been invited following the National Competitive Bidding Procedure for widening and improvement of the section of the Kandy-Jaffna Road spanning from CH 58+240km to CH 63+000 km. Eight (08) bids have been received for the same. Based on the recommendations made by the High Level Procurement Committee and the Procurement Appeal Board following the evaluation of the said bids, the proposal made by the Minister of Transport, Highways, and Urban Development to award the said contract to M/s Tudawe Brothers (Pvt) Ltd., the substantially responsive lowest bidder for a sum of Rs.1.070 billion (inclusive of contingency funds and exclusive of Value Added Tax), was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Obtaining Financial Assistance from the Asian Development Bank for the implementation of the ‘Skills Development System Transformation Programme’
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-10-12 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Approval has been granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2026-08-24, to authorize the Department of External Resources to conduct negotiations with the Asian Development Bank to secure financial assistance for the implementation of the 'Skills Development Systems Transformation Programme.' Accordingly, the Department of External Resources has taken necessary steps to hold formal loan negotiations with the Asian Development Bank on 2026-08-25, to obtain a facility worth US$ 100 million in support of the sectorial strategic plan aimed at developing an effective technical and vocational education and training system. The proposed loan facility comprises US$ 50 million from Concessional Ordinary Capital Resources and US$ 50 million from Regular Ordinary Capital Resources under the Results‑based Financing Modality. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. President, in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning, and Economic Development, to obtain a Results-based Financing Facility of US$ 100 million from the Asian Development Bank for the implementation of the 'Skills Development Systems Transformation Programme’, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Obtaining a Grant Assistance from the Government of Japan to improve the Pump Station on the Kelani River Basin
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-10-12 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Government of Japan has agreed to provide a grant aid of 2.179 billion Japanese Yen (approximately 4.56 billion Sri Lankan Rupees) to implement the project for upgrading the pumping station in the Kelani River basin. The proposed project for the Improvement of the Pump Station aims to mitigate flood risks in the Mudun Ela sub-basin covering Wattala and Peliyagoda areas, facilitate sustainable urban development, and create developable land for national economic activities. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. President, in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning, and Economic Development, to sign the Exchange of Note with the Government of Japan and the Grant Agreement with the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) to secure the proposed grant, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Awarding the contract for the supply of Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) for Litro Gas Lanka Limited for the year 2027
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-10-12 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Bids have been invited following the International Competitive Bidding Procedure to procure 420,000 (±20%) MT of LPG (Liquefied Petroleum Gas) for Litro Gas Lanka Limited. Four (04) bids have been received for the same. Based on the recommendation made by the High Level Procurement Committee, following the evaluation of the said bids,  the proposal made by the Hon. President, in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development, to award the contract for the supply of 420,000 MT (±20%) of LPG (Liquefied Petroleum Gas) (with a guaranteed minimum quantity of 336,000 MT) for a period of 12 months commencing from  2027-01-01, to M/s OQ Trading Limited, the substantially responsive lowest bidder at a total value comprising the Saudi Aramco contract price + US$ 133.93 per MT (on Cost, Insurance and Freight basis), was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Provision of the stationery allowance to the school children for the school year 2027
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-10-12 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The School Stationery Allowance Programme has been in operation since 2025. Accordingly, the Cabinet was informed by the Hon. President in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning, and Economic Development that steps are being taken to directly transfer the School Stationery Allowance of Rs.6,000 to the bank accounts of 1,000,000 students from families enrolled in the 'Aswesuma' programme for the year 2027, and to provide vouchers worth Rs.6,000 to 500,000 children identified by the Ministry of Education, Higher Education, and Vocational Education under the same programme and the Cabinet granted its concurrence for the same.

description: Securing additional provisions under the Re-energizing of the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Loan Scheme (Re-MSME Plus)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-10-12 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Re-energizing of the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Loan Scheme (Re-MSME Plus) Loan Scheme was implemented in this year by consolidating the Re-MSME Loan Scheme with several selected ongoing loan programmes. Approvals have been granted to implement projects relating to the value of Rs.4,276.50 million to uplift businesses affected by the 'Ditwah' disaster situation and projects relating to the value of Rs.25,926.84 million for other micro, small and medium-scale enterprises, at the end of August 2026. Provisions amounting to Rs.30,000 million had been provided for the Re‑MSME Plus Loan Scheme and the entire amount has been utilized by participating financial institutions by now. Participating financial institutions have reported a requirement for additional provisions of approximately Rs.7,500 million for projects that have completed the internal appraisal process and obtained loan approvals, and are ready for loan disbursement. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. President, in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development, to provide additional provisions of Rs.7,500 million, enabling to continue to grant loans under the said loan scheme, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Construction of a Student Hostel, Workshops and Cafeteria for the University of Vocational Technology, Ratmalana
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-10-12 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Approval was granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2017-01-03, to implement the Project for constructing a student hostel with accommodation facilities for 600 students, modern teaching workshops, and a canteen with a seating capacity of 300 for the University of Vocational Technology in Ratmalana. Nevertheless, implementation of the project was delayed due to changes in planning and procurement activities, the economic crisis and various other factors and subsequently, steps were taken to temporarily suspend the Project in 2022 in line with the Government policy of restricting capital expenditure. A problematic situation has arisen by now with regard to the fulfillment of students' welfare and educational needs due to the inadequacy of hostel, workshops and canteen facilities of the University. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister, in her capacity as the Minister of Education, Higher Education and Vocational Education, to resume and implement the said Project within the premises of the University of Vocational Technology in Ratmalana, under a revised total cost estimate of Rs. 3,380 million within the Medium Term Budgetary Framework of 2027-2029, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Strategic Diversification of the State Printing Corporation through a Public Private Partnership
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-10-12 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The State Printing Corporation, which was established in the year 1968, functions as the primary state entity for printing school textbooks, official government publications, and documents of Government institutions. Although the Corporation has consistently recorded financial profits in recent years, challenges regarding production efficiency and cost competitiveness have arisen due to the deterioration of machinery and outdated printing technology. Accordingly, restructuring its business model and technical capabilities has become essential to ensure the long-term sustainability of the Corporation. Taking into account these matters, the feasibility of implementing a strategic diversification programme titled 'Smart Print Initiative' has been identified, aiming to transform the State Printing Corporation into a high-security printing entity driven by modern technology. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister, in her capacity as the Minister of Education, Higher Education and Vocational Education, to implement the proposed Diversification Programme under a Public-Private Partnership framework, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Establishment of Co-Financing Scheme for Commercialization of Research and Development Innovations with High Commercialization Potential and Large – Scale Capital Requirements
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-10-12 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Measures are being taken by the National Initiative for Research and Development Commercialization (NIRDC), to provide grants and concessionary loan facilities for the effective commercialization of research and development innovations in Sri Lanka. Accordingly, under Project Category 01, a full grant up to Rs.10 million is provided for the commercialization of Research and Development Projects with high commercialization potential and small-scale capital requirements. Under Project Category 02, a grant of Rs.10 million together with a concessionary loan of up to Rs.40 million at a concessionary interest rate of 3% is provided through banks for the commercialization of Research and Development Projects requiring medium-scale capital. In addition, the suitability of implementing a co-financing scheme of up to Rs.500 million has been identified to be implemented as Project Category 03 for the commercialization of Research and Development Projects with high commercialization potential and require large-scale capital. Under the proposed financing scheme, plans are in place to provide loans of up to Rs.450 million through commercial banks with an interest subsidy of 5% to cover additional capital requirements, in addition to the above the Rs. 10 million grant and the loan of up to Rs.40 million at a concessionary interest rate of 3%. Accordingly, the proposal made by the President to implement the proposed Financing Scheme, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Declaration of the Nakolagane Sanctuary under the Fauna and Flora Protection Ordinance
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-10-12 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Several Private Companies had utilized approximately 1,500 acres of land, which had remained as forests for some time, located in the Galgamuwa Divisional Secretariat Division of the Kurunegala District, for activities such as cash crop cultivation, mineral mining and soil excavation. Several environmental organizations have filed a petition in the Supreme Court seeking to halt to these activities, citing the environmental damage caused by the deforestation and the exacerbation of the human-elephant conflict in the North Western Province. Delivering its Judgment on the petition, the Supreme Court ordered that the entire area comprising of the 55 hectares of cleared land as well as the remaining forest sections be declared either a sanctuary or an elephant management reserve under section 2(2) of the Fauna and Flora Protection Ordinance. In accordance with the said Order, through a joint survey conducted by the Department of Survey and the Department of Wildlife Conservation, a land area of ​​682 hectares has been identified to be declared a wildlife sanctuary. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Environment to declare the said land area to the extent of 682 hectare area including the maximum water level of the nearby Palukadawala Tank, as the Nakolagane Sanctuary, as per the provisions of the Fauna and Flora Protection Ordinance and with the concurrence of the Department of Irrigation, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Vesting the Roads not belonging to the Road Development Authority to the said Authority and formulating a proper mechanism for their maintenance
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-10-12 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Taking into account proposals submitted by District Coordinating Committees, approval was granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2026-07-20, to appoint a Committee chaired by an Additional Secretary of the Ministry of Transport, Highways and Urban Development for making recommendations with regard to transferring roads currently maintained by Provincial Councils or Local Authorities but not belonging to the Road Development Authority, to the Road Development Authority, as well as securing the necessary funds and staff for their maintenance. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Transport, Highways and Urban Development to take further steps to declare roads currently under the authority of other institutions as National Highways, based on recommendations from Road Acquisition Committee of the Road Development Authority, following an assessment of basic eligibility, technical feasibility, and relevant criteria with regard to requests made to upgrade said roads, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Securing financial facilities for the Water Supply and Sanitation Reform Programme
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-10-12 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Approval was granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2026-03-16, to obtain a Policy Based Lending of US$ 620 million from the Asian Development Bank under 05 Sub‑programmes to continue Sri Lanka’s reform agenda in parallel with Extended Fund Facility programme of the International Monetary Fund. It has been planned to implement the Water Supply and Sanitation Reform Programme - Sub‑programme 2 utilizing US$ 100 million of the said loan amount.  The programme aims to assist the Government of Sri Lanka in addressing the challenges such as weak water resource management, operational and financial inefficiencies, exposure to climate risks, social inclusion gaps and fragmented stakeholder coordination through comprehensive reform measures. Accordingly, the proposal made by the President, in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development, to enter into an Agreement with the Asian Development Bank to obtain the said Policy Based Lending facility, comprising US$ 50 million from the regular ordinary capital resources of the Bank and US$ 50 million from its Concessional Ordinary Capital Resources, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Signing of a Memorandum of Understanding between the Asia‑Pacific Accreditation and Certification Commission and the Tertiary and Vocational Education Commission of Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-10-12 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - A Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was previously signed between the Asia-Pacific Accreditation and Certification Commission based in the Philippines and the Tertiary and Vocational Education Commission of Sri Lanka, with the aim of strengthening accreditation practices within the Technical and Vocational Education and Training System of Sri Lanka. As the validity period of the said MoU, which was signed for a period of 05 years has now expired, a proposal has been made to sign a new MoU in that regard. The proposed Memorandum of Understanding aims to achieve several objectives: strengthening regional ties and cooperation in vocational education, securing support from the Asia Pacific Accreditation and Certification Commission (APACC) for the advancement of vocational education in Sri Lanka, promoting APACC accreditation and certification of vocational training institutions, further strengthening the National Vocational Qualification Framework of Sri Lanka, appointing a National Accreditation Coordinator for Sri Lanka and identifying potential local accreditation personnel who could be trained in APACC procedures and standards for future accreditation activities. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister, in her capacity as the Minister of Education, Higher Education and Vocational Education, for both parties to sign the said MoU, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Appointment to act in the Post of Director General of the Department of National Botanic Gardens on full time basis
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-10-05 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Ms. H.C.P. Jayaweera, who served as the Director General of the Department of National Botanic Gardens, retired from the public service upon reaching the age of 60 on 2026-09-14. Therefore, the proposal made by the Minister of Environment to appoint Mr. M.M.D.J. Senarathna, the senior most Officer in Grade I of the Sri Lanka Scientific Service currently serving in the said Department to act in the vacant post of Director General of the Department of National Botanic Gardens on a full-time basis, with immediate effect, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Introducing the Fauna and Flora (Regulating Activities of Adi Wasi Communities within Designated Areas) Regulations
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-10-05 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Aiming to safeguard the traditional livelihoods and ecosystems of indigenous communities, the need has been identified to introduce a formal regulatory mechanism that ensures their engagement in livelihood activities by being more sensitive to existing laws. Accordingly, Fauna and Flora (Regulating Activities of Adi Wasi Communities within Designated Areas) Regulations have been drafted under the Fauna and Flora Protection Ordinance (Chapter 469) for permitting any registered member of the indigenous community to engage in designated activities within the relevant areas in order to protect the rights acquired through law, custom, usage, or traditional practice that are fundamental to the survival of indigenous people and are exercised on a state land. The proposal made by the Minister of Environment to publish the said Regulations in the Government Gazette and subsequently present the same in Parliament, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Formulation of an Institutional Framework for the establishment of the Upper Watershed Area Management Authority
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-10-05 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Policy approval of the Cabinet has been granted at the meeting held on 2026-06-08 to establish the Upper Watershed Area Management Authority to identify and implement a systematic, long-term programme to protect the central highlands including upper watershed areas ensuring resilience against adverse climatic impacts caused by natural disasters and human activities, while also facilitating the country's sustainable development. Accordingly, a concept paper outlining the proposed institutional structure, duties, powers, and functional scope, and governance and coordination mechanisms has been prepared by the Technical Expert Committee appointed by the Secretary to the President. Based on the said concept paper, the Cabinet approved the proposal made by the President to instruct the Legal Draftsman to draft a bill containing the necessary legal provisions for the establishment of the Upper Watershed Area Management Authority.

description: Supply and laying of HDPE distribution pipelines, providing service connections and construction of 250 cubic meters capacity water tower for Community Based Organizations of the Medawachchiya and Rambewa Divisional Secretariat Divisions of the Anuradhapura North Water Supply Project- Phase II
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-10-05 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Under the Anuradhapura North Water Supply Project-Phase II implemented with the financial assistance of the Japan International Cooperation Agency, the National Water Supply and Drainage Board has planned to provide safe drinking water to the residents of Medawachchiya and Rambewa by constructing an elevated water tower with a capacity of 250 cubic meters and laying a 425-kilometer pipeline network to serve 17,000 water connections. For the purpose, bids have been invited in 2022 by following the National Competitive Bidding Procedure, with the concurrence of the Japan International Cooperation Agency, to select a suitable contractor. However, the procurement process could not proceed due to the economic crisis prevailed in the country. Considering the time required to re-invite bids, the JICA has proposed proceeding with the procurement using the bids already submitted and applying price adjustments in accordance with relevant regulations. Accordingly, based on the recommendations made by the High-Level Procurement Committee following the evaluation of bids submitted by three bidders who had agreed to extend the validity period of their bid securities, the proposal made by the Minister of Housing, Construction and Water Supply to award the said contract to M/s Sierra Construction Ltd., the substantially responsive lowest bidder for a sum of 600.11 million Japanese Yen and 1.76 billion Sri Lankan Rupees, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Awarding Special Project status for the Kerawalapitiya - Colombo Port Second Underground Cable Project under the Value Added Tax Act, No.14 of 2002
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-10-05 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Approval has been granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2021-09-13 to implement the second 220kV underground cable project extending from Kerawalapitiya to the Colombo Port, in accordance with the Long-Term Transmission Plan of the country under funding from the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank. Accordingly, the contract for the implementation of the said project was awarded by the then Ceylon Electricity Board to the selected contractor, the consortium comprising M/s Jiangsu ETERN Co. Ltd. (China) and LS Cable & System Limited (LS Cable Korea), following the formal procurement procedure. As of now, the project has been transferred to National Transmission Network Service Provider (Private) Limited, a successor company to the Ceylon Electricity Board. Recognizing the strategic importance of the project, the Cabinet approved the proposal made by the Minister of Energy to designate the second 220kV underground cable project from Kerawalapitiya to the Colombo Port as a Special Project under the provisions of the Value Added Tax Act, No.14 of 2002, in order to secure the necessary exemptions from the payment of Value Added Tax, customs import duties, and other relevant taxes, levies, and charges.

description: Procurement of medicines required to maintain health services
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-10-05 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Bids have been invited following the international competitive bidding procedure for the procurement of the following essential medicines required to maintain health services of the general public. description: Awarding of the Contract for the extension of the existing Quay Wall and the Construction of the Access Road and Boundary Wall at the Valaichchenai Fishery Harbour, and its Construction Supervision Consultancy Services Contract
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-10-05 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Approval has been granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2025-08-04 to implement the project for extending the existing quay wall and constructing the access road and boundary wall at the Valaichchenai Fishery Harbour. Bids were invited following the formal procurement guidelines to select a contractor to carry out construction activities of the project, and two (02) bids have been received for the same. Following the evaluation of said bids, the Procurement Committee of the Ministry has recommended to award the contract to M/s Senok Trade Combine (Pvt) Limited, the substantially responsive lowest bidder for a sum of Rs.766.88 million (excluding Value Added Tax). Bids have also been invited to select a consultancy firm for the construction supervision consultancy services of the project by following the formal procurement guidelines, and three (03) bids have been received for the same. Following the evaluation of the said bids, the Ministerial Consultants Procurement Committee recommended awarding the consultancy services contract to M/s EML Consultant PLC, the substantially responsive lowest bidder for a sum of Rs.35.54 million (excluding Value Added Tax). Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Fisheries, Aquatic and Ocean Resources to award the said contracts, based on the recommendations of the Ministerial Procurement Committee and the Ministerial Consultants Procurement Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Deployment of a new vessel for the Delft-Jaffna Sea Route under the ‘Praja Shakthi’ National Programme
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-10-05 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Due to the inadequacy of facilities for the transportation of a large number of passengers safely on a single trip in the Jaffna Peninsula, particularly between the mainland and outlying islands like Delft, maintaining passenger marine transportation has become challenging. As a solution, the appropriateness of deploying a sea ferry capable of carrying approximately 150 passengers on the Delft-Jaffna Sea Route under the 'Praja Shakthi' National Programme has been identified. Accordingly, the Cabinet approved the proposal made by the Minister of Fisheries, Aquatic and Marine Resources to have the ferry manufactured by Cey-Nor Foundation Ltd., to operate the vessel through the Delft Development Society (established under the Department of Samurdhi Development), and to utilize the generated revenue for the livelihood development of all low-income residents in the Delft area, including the society's members.

description: Carrying out a feasibility study to minimize the traffic congestion at the Lotus Intersection, Port Access Elevated Highway and Marine Drive Connectivity and surrounding areas
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-10-05 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Road Development Authority has called for Expressions of Interest to select a Consultancy Agency to carry out a feasibility study aimed at alleviating traffic congestion at the Lotus Intersection, Port Access Elevated Highway and Marine Drive Connectivity and surrounding areas. Following the shortlisting of the submitted Expressions of Interest for the same, Requests for Proposals were issued to 05 entities. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Transport, Highways and Urban Development based on the recommendation submitted by the Cabinet Appointed Consultants Procurement Committee on the said proposals, to award the said Consultancy Contract to M/s Master Hellie's Engineering Consultants (Pvt) Ltd. for a sum of Rs.91.21 million (excluding VAT) comprising a Local Component of Rs.52.44 million (excluding VAT) and a Foreign Component of US$ 122,859, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of the Road Infrastructure Improvement Projects
